hints.title: Find the turning heights
hints.body: Differentiate the cubic and solve for its stationary inputs. Substitute them into the original cubic to express the two turning heights in terms of a.
hints.recap: Stationary points can separate the crossings of a cubic graph.
hints.pitfall: The derivative gives the input positions; substitute into the function for the heights.
hints.pause: Sketch the cubic using its end behaviour and the two turning heights.

recall.reminder: Stationary points can separate the crossings of a cubic graph.

hints.title: Include the touching cases
hints.body: Move the cubic up and down as a changes. Count its distinct roots when both turns are on one side of the axis, when they straddle it, and when a turn lies on it.
hints.recap: A repeated root at a touch is still one distinct solution.
hints.pitfall: A turning point on the axis may leave another crossing elsewhere.
hints.pause: Find exactly which values of a give one distinct real solution.

recall.reminder: Count a touching root once when finding distinct real roots.

hints.title: Test the whole set allowed by each option
hints.body: An option is sufficient if every a it allows lies in your one-solution set.
hints.recap: A sufficient condition may be stronger than necessary.
hints.pitfall: One allowed value giving the wrong number of roots disproves sufficiency.
hints.pause: Check every option, including its boundary values.

recall.reminder: A sufficient condition may be stronger than necessary.

solution:
For F(x)=x3−3x2+a, F′(x)=3x(x−2). The local maximum is F(0)=a and the local minimum is F(2)=a−4. The cubic has exactly one real root when both turning heights are negative (a<0) or both positive (a>4).

For 0<a<4 there are three distinct crossings. At a=0, F=x2(x−3); at a=4, F=(x−2)2(x+1). Each boundary therefore has two distinct real roots.

The condition |a|>4 means a<−4 or a>4, entirely inside the successful range, so it is sufficient. The other listed conditions each permit a boundary or interior value in [0, 4].

Answer E.
knowledgePattern: Derive a cubic root-count range then recognise a sufficient subset
